definitions.explanation: The capacity to adjust to new conditions, environments, or situations. Used for both people and organisms.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{適応力|てきおうりょく}が{高|たか}い。
{子供|こども}は{大人|おとな}より{適応力|てきおうりょく}があると{言|い}われている。
examples.english: Children are said to be more adaptable than adults.

examples.japanese: {海外|かいがい}{赴任|ふにん}では{語学力|ごがくりょく}だけでなく{異文化|いぶんか}への{適応力|てきおうりょく}も{求|もと}められる。
examples.english: Overseas assignments require not only language skills but also the ability to adapt to different cultures.

notes:
A compound of {適応|てきおう} (adaptation) and {力|りょく} (power, ability). Follows the productive Japanese pattern of adding {力|りょく} to abstract nouns to form 'ability to X.'

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {順応力|じゅんのうりょく} is a close synonym, slightly more passive
- {柔軟性|じゅうなんせい} means flexibility, a related quality

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {適応力|てきおうりょく}が{高|たか}い (highly adaptable)
- {適応力|てきおうりょく}がある (to have adaptability)
- {適応力|てきおうりょく}に{優|すぐ}れた (excellent in adaptability)
- {環境|かんきょう}への{適応力|てきおうりょく} (adaptability to the environment)
